describes: The sizes and bounds of the agent workflows, and what each lets its agents see: the review that `.claude/workflows/build-change-task.js` runs on each task of a product change and the kinds of task it holds to a red run (`buildReview*`, `buildRedFirstKinds`); the kinds it gives an independent test-builder, what that agent may read, where its tests live, which of them its architect runs and how often (`buildIndependentKinds`, `independentInputs`, `independentTestDir`, `independentLayers`, `architectRunLayers`, `buildArchitectMaxRounds`), and which stage of those tests runs at a push (`independentBuildStage`), where `scripts/check-thresholds.mjs` reads `independentTestDir` and `independentBuildStage` too; the sizes of the scenario trace that `.claude/workflows/verify-change-trace.js` takes of a change at verify (`verifyTrace*`); the markers, thresholds and skeptic counts of the batched prompt review, the heading a run's analysis lists its loaded prompts under and the label of the line holding its session id, the window, floor, cut-off, not-viable share and table of prompts no analysed run loads that `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` counts loads by, the floor and not-viable share of its fix-recurrence rate, and the lenses and repetitions of its stored decision cases (`promptReview*`; `.claude/skills/close-prompt-run/SKILL.md` and `.claude/agents/continuous-prompt-improvement.md`), which `.claude/workflows/review-prompts.js` and `.claude/workflows/author-prompt-cases.js` also read; and the bounds on a review or design workflow a session writes itself (`session*`; `CLAUDE.md` § A workflow a session writes itself is bounded), and on the fixes a session makes against one failure whose cause it is finding (`rootCauseMaxFixes`; `.claude/skills/root-cause/SKILL.md` § 6). The `promptReviewMatch*` keys are the thresholds and the `none` option of the TypeSafe match that `scripts/match-held-findings.mjs` makes, before the prompt review's workflow runs, between each new finding and the findings earlier reviews hold. `promptReviewProseMinProbability` is the probability at which an answer to a prose decision case meets it, which `scripts/grade-prose-cases.mjs` reads when the session grades the answers the prompt review's workflow returns. The trace's clause run also reads, among the `verifyTrace*` keys, the probability under which an answer of `scripts/judge-trace-clauses.mjs` sends a traced row to the skeptics (`verifyTraceClauseThreshold`), which that script reads too.
whyThisFileExists: Each value decides how much rigour a workflow buys or how many agents it spends, and is read by a workflow script and by the prompt that runs it, so it has one home, which both cite by key (`CLAUDE.md` § Three kinds of file, and never a fourth). These are the workflow's tunable choices: the spellings every stage agrees on are `tools/policy/vocabulary.json`'s, and what a person alone may change is `tools/policy/pr-review.json`'s and `tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json`'s (`docs/decisions.md` § D-27). The `promptReview*` keys stay together because the prompt reviewer reads them by prefix. `rootCauseMaxFixes` is read by a skill alone, no workflow script; it is here because it bounds a session's own work, as the `session*` keys do, and a record of its own would split those bounds across two.

It holds `buildRedFirstKinds` the same way: it stops as `not-red` a task of each kind the key lists whose builder returns neither a red record nor an already-green report for a named scenario, runs such a task of each kind it does not list on to review, and refuses a kind that is not an `assetLabels` key. No gate holds `sessionReviewMaxFindings`, `sessionReviewSkeptics` or `sessionWorkflowMaxAgents`: a session reads them when it writes a review or design workflow of its own, which no gate sees, and `CLAUDE.md` names the keys and spells none of their values. whatItDoesNOTDo: It does not hold a rule about how a run proceeds, which lives in CLAUDE.md or in the skill that runs it: how a session finds a failure's cause, and what it reports once `rootCauseMaxFixes` fixes have failed, is `.claude/skills/root-cause/SKILL.md`, how a run writes its analysis and when a review of the analyses starts is `.claude/skills/close-prompt-run/SKILL.md`, the form of each line a run or a review writes in the tracker is the header of `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs`, and how a review counts a finding and applies the threshold is `.claude/agents/continuous-prompt-improvement.md` § 3. It retires no prompt: `promptReviewUnloadedPrompts` only keeps a prompt out of the candidates `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` prints, and a person decides a retirement (`.claude/skills/retire-asset/SKILL.md`). It does not say which branch gets a review a session writes itself, or that no effort level raises its bounds: that is `CLAUDE.md` § A workflow a session writes itself is bounded, and this file holds only the three numbers it names, which nothing here runs or checks. It holds no prompt text: the review's lens prompts, the kinds of finding they report and the red run a builder is asked for and the routes its architect gives a failure are the build workflow's own, how the test-builder writes a test is `.claude/agents/test-builder.md`, what the parent does when that workflow stops is `.claude/skills/change-build/SKILL.md` § 3. Build it, and prove it, the trace's design lenses are the change-verify session's, what a gap is is `.claude/skills/change-verify/SKILL.md` § 4. Every scenario is traced, the questions a prompt review's skeptics answer are `.claude/workflows/review-prompts.js`'s own, a lens's text is `.claude/workflows/author-prompt-cases.js`'s, what a stored case holds is `.claude/prompt-cases/README.md`'s, and what a finding blocks is `.claude/skills/change-build/SKILL.md` § 5. What the build turns up. It holds no spelling every stage agrees on, which is `tools/policy/vocabulary.json`'s, and no prompt's word budget, which is `tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json`'s.

buildReviewLensesMeans: The reviewers `.claude/workflows/build-change-task.js` runs on one task of a product change, chosen by what the task mainly changes: each key an `assetLabels` key, each value the lens keys, one reviewer each. The parent session picks the key (`.claude/skills/change-build/SKILL.md` § 3. Build it, and prove it). The lens prompts are the workflow's own, and a task adds only its focus to them, so no run reviews through more lenses than its set. `asset:spec` has no set: a task never edits its own delta specs, and a spec revision is the parent's, under that skill's § 5. A documentation, register or prompt task runs at most two lenses: the register-and-briefing task asdlc-openspec-zgh.6 ran three and spent 35 agents and 2,946,105 tokens to confirm 2 of the 9 findings it sent to skeptics, both minor (wf_f256bc20-ffb, a workflow state file outside this repository). A new key must be an `assetLabels` key, and a lens must exist in the workflow's library before a set names it; mise run workflows:selftest runs a clean control for every key and refuses a lens the workflow does not have. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-d6b).
buildReviewSkepticsMeans: How many skeptics the workflow sends to confirm one finding of each severity. Each judges the finding against the delta specs, the design and the task, and answers upheld, refuted or unverified; a majority of those sent decides, and a finding with no majority goes back to the parent as unverified, never as refuted (the workflow's header holds the mechanics). A spec contradiction is always confirmed at `blocker`, because a confirmed one halts the run. The calculator change (asdlc-openspec-zgh) sent every finding to three: 58 findings went to 174 skeptics and 19 were upheld, and all 16 that its build runs confirmed were minor (the session's wf_*.json workflow state files, outside this repository; the figures are re-derived in a note on asdlc-openspec-d6b). Lowering `blocker` below 3 lets one vote halt the run on a spec contradiction. Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-d6b). `major` lowered from 3 to 1 on 2026-09-28 by D-16 (asdlc-openspec-hsg), item 3, which the maintainer chose over the recommendation to leave this key for asdlc-openspec-j09.11 to resize with the pilot's figures; `blocker` and `minor` stay. Where it loses: one vote now decides whether a major finding is confirmed, fixed and earns another round, where a majority of three would outvote a skeptic that misreads it.
buildReviewMaxRoundsMeans: The most review rounds one run of the workflow makes. A round reviews, confirms and fixes, and the next reviews that fix; after the last round's fix the run stops and reports the fix as unreviewed, and the parent reads its diff. In the calculator change no round after the second confirmed anything: its two third rounds sent 2 findings to skeptics and confirmed none (wf_ad92e5b6-d54 and wf_2d38608d-3a8, workflow state files outside this repository). Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-d6b).
buildReviewMajorSeveritiesMeans: The severities of a confirmed defect that earn another review round. A round that confirms none of these is the last: its confirmed minor defects are fixed and the run stops, so review does not loop on small findings, as `.claude/skills/change-build/SKILL.md` § 5. What the build turns up keeps it from looping on coverage. No build run of the calculator change confirmed a finding above minor, yet five of them ran a second round and two a third (the session's wf_*.json workflow state files, outside this repository). Decided 2026-09-25 (asdlc-openspec-d6b).
buildRedFirstKindsMeans: The kinds of task, each an `assetLabels` key, held to the red run: `.claude/workflows/build-change-task.js` asks every builder to see each scenario the task names fail before it changes the code under test, and stops a run of a kind listed here as `not-red`, before any review, when the builder returns neither a red record nor an already-green report for one of them (its header holds the mechanics; `docs/decisions.md` § D-14). A task of a kind not listed, a docs, prompt, register, environment, tool or gate task today, is asked for the same records and not held to them. Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-fye): `asset:product`, `asset:tool` and `asset:gate`, the kinds whose proofs are commands, were proposed, and the maintainer chose `asset:product` alone. Where that loses: a gate's new selftest case that passes before the refusal it holds exists is not caught by a red run, only later by the honesty lens. Adding `asset:tool` loses where a tool task only renames a flag: it has no proof that can fail first, so its builder reports it already green and the parent judges it. mise run workflows:selftest stops as `not-red` a task of each kind listed here whose builder returns neither record for a named scenario, runs such a task of each kind not listed on to review, and refuses a kind that is not an `assetLabels` key.
buildIndependentKindsMeans: The kinds of task, each an `assetLabels` key, for which `.claude/workflows/build-change-task.js` runs the test-builder beside the builder and then the architect's runs of its tests (the workflow's header holds the mechanics; `docs/test-strategy.md` § Build Agents; `docs/decisions.md` § D-13, items 16 and 17). A task of a kind listed here must name its app (`args.app`). A kind not listed is built and reviewed as before, with no independent test. `asset:product` alone, since the product's code under `apps/` is what a Binding Surface and a contract describe. Where it loses: an `asset:tool` task that changes a script an app's tests run through gets no independent test. mise run workflows:selftest runs a task of this kind through the test-builder and the architect, and refuses a kind that is not an `assetLabels` key. Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-j09.11).
buildArchitectMaxRoundsMeans: The most runs of the test-builder's tests one run of the workflow makes. Each run triages every failing file into one route and, but for the last, acts on the routes: one fixer for the fix-app routes, and the test-builder again for the rewrite-test ones; the last run's failures are triaged and returned, and stop the run as `architect-failing`. So 2 is one fix or rewrite and a second run to see it hold. It is a choice, not a measurement: no change has yet run the architect's triage. Where it loses: a failure whose fix needs a second attempt stops the run for the parent, where 3 would have tried again. mise run workflows:selftest stops a run whose tests fail at every run as `architect-failing` after this many. Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-j09.11).
independentInputsMeans: Everything the test-builder may read, as paths under the change's worktree, `{change}` and `{app}` filled in from the workflow's arguments: the proposal, the design, the delta specs, the app's Binding Surface, its contract artifacts and fitness records, its own earlier tests, and the header of scripts/test-trace.mjs, the home of the convention its tests follow. A path names a file or every file under a directory. A script is given as its header alone, its first block comment, since a header is where a rule lives and the code below it is not the test-builder's to read. The epic's children come from the tracker beside them, without their notes (`docs/test-strategy.md` § Shared inputs). The test-builder has no tool, so what is not given here it never sees; the workflow drops any path Setup returns outside these and logs it. Adding a path lets the test-builder see what the app-builder may have written: never add a path under `apps/` outside these. Where it loses: a living spec the change leaves alone is not given, so a test of a MODIFIED scenario sees only its new text. mise run workflows:selftest drops a planted path outside these from the test-builder's prompt. Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-j09.11).
independentTestDirMeans: Where the test-builder's tests live, `{app}` filled in: below it a directory per stage, `build` for a test at a layer of `architectRunLayers` that runs at build and `verify` for every other, then one per layer of `independentLayers`, each test a `<name>.test.js`. Ownership is this path prefix: the workflow stops as `not-independent` a builder or fixer whose changed files enter it for any app, and a test-builder file outside it or under the wrong stage. `mise run calculator:test` does not reach it, since its pattern is not recursive; `mise run calculator:test:independent` runs its `build` stage at each push and in CI, and `mise run calculator:test:verify` its `verify` stage, which change-verify's fresh run, scripts/fresh-run.mjs, runs at Verify (asdlc-openspec-j09.14), so no E2E test or Verify-deferred fitness function runs at a push (`docs/test-strategy.md` § Build exit criteria). Moving it strands every test under the old path until they move with it. `mise run thresholds:check` reads it too (the header of `scripts/check-thresholds.mjs`): it refuses a policy without it, and leaves a `--dir` under any stage of it but the one `independentBuildStage` names, which is the Verify stage's, out of its coverage run and the Routines' mutation run (asdlc-openspec-8yd). Where it loses: an app-builder's own consumer-side contract test lives outside it, so a count of contract tests by directory undercounts, where a count by the tests' metadata would not. Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-j09.11).
independentBuildStageMeans: The name of the stage directory under `independentTestDir` whose tests run at a push: a test at a layer of `architectRunLayers` declared to run at build. Every other stage's tests run at Verify (`docs/test-strategy.md` § Build exit criteria). `mise run thresholds:check` (`scripts/check-thresholds.mjs`) reads it: a `--dir` under this stage runs in its coverage run and the Routines' mutation run, a `--dir` under any other stage of `independentTestDir` runs in neither, and a policy without this key is refused. `.claude/workflows/build-change-task.js` (`stageOf`, and `${I.dir}/build/`) and the `--dir` of `tasks.toml`'s `calculator:test:independent` still spell it, and nothing holds them to this key, until asdlc-openspec-d9rt. So changing it here alone strands the build stage: the gate takes the directory the workflow writes to for a Verify stage and runs none of its tests. The name is the one asdlc-openspec-j09.11 gave the stage on 2026-09-29 (98f6813); the key came with asdlc-openspec-8yd on 2026-10-03, so that the gate does not spell it a second time.
independentLayersMeans: The layers the test-builder writes, each a `testTraceLayers` key and a directory under `independentTestDir`, as `docs/test-strategy.md` § Test ownership gives them to it; every other layer is the app-builder's, and an architect may ask the app-builder for a lower-layer test only at one of those. Adding a layer here gives it to the test-builder and takes it from the app-builder. Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-j09.11).
architectRunLayersMeans: The layers of `independentLayers` whose tests the workflow's architect runs against the build after the review, as `docs/test-strategy.md` § Test ownership has it: contract tests and the fitness functions whose execution environment is `build`. An E2E test is written and returned, and runs at Verify. Adding `e2e` runs every journey after every task, which the strategy leaves to the verifier. Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-j09.11).
verifyTraceMaxScenariosMeans: The most scenarios one tracer of `.claude/workflows/verify-change-trace.js` traces. The change-verify session groups a change's scenarios, whole requirements of one capability where they fit, into groups of at most this many, and the workflow runs one tracer per group and refuses a larger group. A tracer reads every proof of its group line by line and runs each, so a larger group is fewer agents and a longer read for each; a change with 61 scenarios, as the calculator change had, needs at least 6 tracers. The maintainer chose it on 2026-09-28 from a recommendation put with the case where it loses, recorded in the notes of asdlc-openspec-as9. Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-as9).
verifyTraceDesignLensesMeans: How many design lenses the workflow runs on a change that has a design.md: the session splits the design's decisions into this many parts, and one agent holds the code to each. A change with no design.md runs none. On a run again after a fix or a rebase, only a lens whose part the diff changes runs again and the others keep their reading, as "Running again" in `.claude/skills/change-verify/SKILL.md` § 4. Every scenario is traced says; the workflow refuses a first run with another number, and a run again whose lenses and kept readings do not add up to it. The calculator change's verify ran 3 (asdlc-openspec-as9). Decided 2026-09-28 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-as9).
verifyTraceSkepticsMeans: How many skeptics the workflow sends to judge each gap, whether a tracer's row shows it or a design lens reports it, but for a proof that failed or did not pass when run, which no vote clears. Each answers upheld, refuted or unverified; a majority of those sent decides, and a gap with no majority goes back to the session as unverified, never as refuted (the workflow's header holds the mechanics). Every gap blocks the change, so there is no severity to size by, and one count serves. Where it loses: a change with 61 scenarios and 4 gaps runs about 6 tracers, 3 lenses and 12 skeptics, 21 agents, where one skeptic for each gap would run 8 fewer, though a single vote would then decide whether a gap blocks the change (the maintainer's choice of 2026-09-28, in the notes of asdlc-openspec-as9). Decided 2026-09-28 (asdlc-openspec-as9).
verifyTraceClauseThresholdMeans: The probability of yes under which an answer of `scripts/judge-trace-clauses.mjs`, TypeSafe's Noul on whether a traced row's tests set up its scenario and assert one of its THEN, AND or BUT clauses with every value the clause states, makes the row an `unasserted` gap in the trace workflow's clause run, which sends it to the `verifyTraceSkeptics` skeptics (`.claude/workflows/verify-change-trace.js`'s header holds the mechanics; `docs/decisions.md` § D-42). A clause at the threshold is not under it. The workflow applies it in code, from `args.policy`, and the judge's summary applies it to name the rows the clause run will send. Measured 2026-10-05 on `typesafeModel` jev-1.13.0 over the 78 outcome clauses of the 60 living scenarios with a happy test in `artifacts/trace/record.json` at 158b73e, each asked with its test's body and the definitions the body uses: one real clause fell under 0.5, CLS-003's THEN at 0.41, whose test falls back to a free port when the spec's 26680 is taken; the calculator capability's 56 were all at 0.87 or above. Of 188 mutations of those tests, an expected literal changed on its assertion line (55), that line dropped (55) and the clause paired with the next scenario's test (78), 180 fell under 0.5, 165 under 0.4 and 181 under 0.6; some of the 8 at 0.5 or above changed an input the assertion line also holds rather than the expected value. 266 requests took 2,097 ms, sent 50 at a time. The issue's 2026-09-29 run, with the helpers described in one line rather than given, put the calculator's lowest at 0.60 and 0.73, CALC-002's (its notes). At 0.6 the same one real clause is under it and one more mutation is caught; at 0.4 none is under it and 15 fewer are caught. Where it loses: a sound row whose outcome a conditional or a helper in another file asserts, as CLS-003's, costs one round of `verifyTraceSkeptics` skeptics at each verify; and the figures are one model's over one repository's tests, so a person changes this key, and measures it again when `typesafeModel` changes. Decided 2026-10-05 from the issue's 2026-09-29 note, which gave 0.5 (asdlc-openspec-6yt.3).
promptReviewAnalysisMarkerMeans: The word that opens the first line of a run's analysis, a note on the issue or epic the run worked, followed by a space and the run id (the header of `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` gives the form, and `.claude/skills/close-prompt-run/SKILL.md` § 1. Write the analysis, or none, when a run writes one). `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` finds every analysis by it, so it must appear in no other note: changing it strands every analysis written under the old word, which no review then finds, so a change rewrites them or reviews them first. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-08 (asdlc-openspec-lzr).
promptReviewLoadedHeadingMeans: The line, alone, under which a run's analysis lists the prompts the run loaded, one to a line with the commit each was read at, and the version of Claude Code it met; the header of `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` is the one home of their form, since D-48. It gives a reader, and a parser that counts each prompt's loads, one spelling to find the list by: before it, an analysis named its prompts in prose, several to a line, and named no version of Claude Code. Changing it leaves every analysis written under the old spelling unfound by the new one, so a change rewrites them or reads both. It must not open with a marker's word, or an analysis would end at it (the header of `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs`), and `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` refuses one that does. Decided 2026-10-05 by D-44 (asdlc-openspec-r6ha.1), which amends D-08 item 1.
promptReviewSessionLabelMeans: The word that opens the line, straight after the `claude --version` line of a run's analysis, that holds the run's Claude Code session id as `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` holds it, a lower-case UUID. The header of `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` gives the form, and `.claude/skills/close-prompt-run/SKILL.md` § 1 says when a run writes it. The id joins a run to its trace in Langfuse, whose `sessionId` is the Claude Code session id (asdlc-openspec-pnp), and `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` carries it in what is pending. The line is optional until a cut-off makes it required (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.7). A line there that opens with the label and holds no session id fails the command, naming its analysis. It must not open with a marker's word, or an analysis would end at it, and `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` refuses one that does. Changing it leaves every analysis written under the old spelling with no session read, so a change rewrites them or reads both. Decided 2026-10-09 by `docs/decisions/asdlc-openspec-ic9h.md` § Decision (asdlc-openspec-ic9h.3), which amends D-44.
promptReviewReadMarkerMeans: The word that opens the line a review appends to an issue for each analysis on it that the review read, followed by a space, the run id, a space, and the review's pull request or `no change` (the header of `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` gives the form). An analysis is pending while no such line names its run id, so changing it makes every analysis already read pending again, and the next review reads them twice. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-08 (asdlc-openspec-lzr); the maintainer chose an appended line over metadata on the issue, with the loss that a hand edit breaking a line miscounts.
promptReviewDueCountMeans: How many pending analyses make a review due, whatever their age; the closing step of every run checks it, and the reviewer checks it again when it starts (`.claude/skills/close-prompt-run/SKILL.md` § 2. Check whether a review is due). It is a choice, not a measurement: eleven review pull requests were opened between 2026-09-24T23:47Z (#28) and 2026-09-25T23:10Z (#53), one per run that proposed a change (`gh pr list --state all --limit 100 --json number,title,createdAt`: the titles from #28 to #53 that cite no issue), so at that pace five analyses pend within about half a day, and each review reads at least that many runs side by side. Raising it makes each batch larger and each review later; 1 reviews every run, as D-05 did. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-08 (asdlc-openspec-lzr).
promptReviewDueAgeDaysMeans: How many days the oldest pending analysis may wait, read from the time in its run id, before a review is due however few are pending. It covers a slow week, when `promptReviewDueCount` analyses take longer to gather. Nothing checks it but the closing step of a run, so in a week when no prompt runs an analysis waits past it for the next run of any prompt; the maintainer chose that over a scheduler (D-08). It is a choice, not a measurement. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-08 (asdlc-openspec-lzr).
promptReviewLoadedSinceMeans: The instant from which `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` holds an analysis to D-44's form: one whose run id's time is at or after it, and holds `promptReviewLoadedHeading`, must list its prompts and its `claude --version` as `.claude/skills/close-prompt-run/SKILL.md` § 1 says, or the command fails, naming it; one before it is prose, not counted, whatever it holds. The value is when D-44 reached the trunk, pull request #152 merged as 9c049b7 (`gh pr view 152 --json mergedAt`). Without it, the first run over the tracker of 2026-10-05 failed on nine analyses written before D-44 that hold the heading's words, "Prompts loaded:", as a prose label over bullets. Moving it earlier fails on those nine; moving it later reads as prose an analysis written in the form, which then loads nothing in the count. Where it loses: a run after it from a checkout that trails the trunk, writing the old prose under the same label, fails the command until a person fixes its lines. Decided 2026-10-05 by D-48 (asdlc-openspec-r6ha.5).
promptReviewLoadWindowDaysMeans: How many days before the newest analysis's time `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` counts each prompt's loads over, the newest included: the analyses in D-44's form in that window are the sample its candidates and the load metric (`count-index.md` § Rates and metrics) rest on. It reads the window from the analyses, never the wall clock, so one tracker gives one answer. Shorter names a prompt that only some work needs, such as a `change-*` skill, after any stretch without that work; longer names a prompt that stopped loading only later, and carries its words in every session meanwhile. The maintainer chose 30 days, Hermes Agent's archive age (`hermes_cli/config_defaults.py` at 667b232), on 2026-10-05 over 14 days and over a window of the last 100 analyses; at the 68 analyses the tracker held from 2026-09-26 to 2026-10-05, about 7 a day, a 30-day window holds about 200. Decided 2026-10-05 by D-48 (asdlc-openspec-r6ha.5).
promptReviewLoadFloorMeans: The fewest analyses in D-44's form in the window under which `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` names no candidate and gives no share for the load metric, only the counts (`CLAUDE.md` § Stateful counts live in `count-index.md`, under a key, its rule on a rate's sample). Lower names a candidate off a few days' runs, such as a prompt that a quiet week did not need; higher holds the first candidates back longer. The maintainer chose 100 on 2026-10-05, with the 30-day window, over 50; at the pace of 2026-09-26 to 2026-10-05, about 7 analyses a day, the first 100 in D-44's form gather about two weeks after it landed. Decided 2026-10-05 by D-48 (asdlc-openspec-r6ha.5).
promptReviewLoadNotViableShareMeans: The share of the prompts with a budget row, less those `promptReviewUnloadedPrompts` names, that no analysis in the window loaded, at or above which `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` reports the load metric at the value `count-index.md` § Rates and metrics gives as meaning the project is not viable, over a window at or above `promptReviewLoadFloor`. At it, most of the prompt words sessions carry serve no run. Lower reads a normal stretch without product work, which leaves the `change-*` skills and their workflows unloaded, as not viable; higher says nothing until most prompts are dead. The maintainer chose a half on 2026-10-05, over a third and over two-thirds; changing it changes that row with it. Decided 2026-10-05 by D-48 (asdlc-openspec-r6ha.5).
promptReviewFixRecurrenceFloorMeans: The fewest exercised fixes, carried lines whose pull request merged and whose key's file a later analysis in D-44's form loaded at a commit descending from the merge commit, under which `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` gives the fix-recurrence metric no rate, only the counts (`count-index.md` § Rates and metrics; `CLAUDE.md` § Stateful counts live in `count-index.md`, under a key, its rule on a rate's sample). At ten, one fix moves the rate by ten points, so a rate at the not-viable line can be one review's bad batch; at twenty, carried lines starting with D-49 keep the rate hidden longer. The maintainer chose 10 on 2026-10-05, over 5 and 20. Decided 2026-10-05 by D-52 (asdlc-openspec-r6ha.8).
promptReviewFixRecurrenceNotViableShareM: The share of exercised fixes a later run shows again, at or above which `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` reports the fix-recurrence metric at the value `count-index.md` § Rates and metrics gives as meaning the project is not viable, over at least `promptReviewFixRecurrenceFloor` exercised fixes. At it, the review's edits fail as often as they hold. At 40%, two in five fixes have failed and the metric still reads viable; a third would read not viable while fixes that held still outnumber those that failed two to one. The maintainer chose a half on 2026-10-05, over a third, the same line as `promptReviewLoadNotViableShare`; changing it changes that row with it. Decided 2026-10-05 by D-52 (asdlc-openspec-r6ha.8).

promptReviewUnloadedPrompts..claude/agents/prompt-case-answerer.md: an agent the prompt review's workflows run by `agentType`, inside the review's own run, which writes no analysis
promptReviewUnloadedPrompts..claude/agents/prompt-case-author.md: an agent the prompt review's workflows run by `agentType`, inside the review's own run, which writes no analysis
promptReviewUnloadedPrompts..claude/agents/test-builder.md: an agent `.claude/workflows/build-change-task.js` runs by `agentType`; the run that called the workflow loads `change-build`, not this file
promptReviewUnloadedPrompts..claude/skills/eli5/SKILL.md: a run that re-explains a reply works no issue, so it writes no analysis (`.claude/skills/close-prompt-run/SKILL.md` § 1)
promptReviewUnloadedPrompts..claude/skills/explore/SKILL.md: a run that thinks a topic through works no issue, so it writes no analysis (`.claude/skills/close-prompt-run/SKILL.md` § 1)

promptReviewUnloadedPrompts..claude/workflows/review-prompts.js: run only by the prompt review's own run, which writes no analysis

promptReviewUnloadedPromptsMeans: The prompts no analysed run loads by design, each keyed by its row in `tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json` with its reason, which `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` never names as a candidate and leaves out of the load metric's share. A run another prompt called, the reviewer's own run and a run that worked no issue write no analysis (`.claude/skills/close-prompt-run/SKILL.md` § 1), and a subagent's file is loaded by the subagent, not by the run whose analysis would list it, so without this table each of these would read as unused and be offered for retirement. A row added here hides that prompt from every count; a row whose prompt has no budget row is refused, since it hides nothing and says what is not so. Decided 2026-10-05 by D-48 (asdlc-openspec-r6ha.5), from the list on that issue and the agents and workflows that reach a run the same way.
promptReviewHeldMarkerMeans: The word that opens a held line, which a review appends to the issue carrying a run's analysis for each finding that run showed and the review did not carry into its pull request: below the threshold, set aside by its file's agent, or on a branch the skeptics did not uphold. Since D-49 it also appends one, beside a closed line, for each finding it carried or closed by its issue, since a key keeps its count and is offered to the next finding only through its held lines (the header of `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` gives the line's form, and `.claude/agents/continuous-prompt-improvement.md` § 6. Mark what was read when a review writes one). The next review counts a finding from these lines, so changing the word strands every count kept under the old one, and each held finding starts again at one; a change rewrites them first. An analysis ends at the next line that opens with any marker, this word among them (the header of `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs`). Decided 2026-09-26 with D-10 (asdlc-openspec-pnm); the maintainer chose a line in the analysis notes, with the loss that a hand edit breaking one resets its count unnoticed.
promptReviewClosedMarkerMeans: The word that opens a closed line, which ends a key the prompt review holds: one carried by a review's pull request, which the review appends for each finding the workflow's `findingsCarried` lists; one an issue owns, such as a finding no prompt owns; or one a person set aside, with the person's reason (the header of `scripts/prompt-runs.mjs` gives the line's form and when it closes a key, and `.claude/agents/continuous-prompt-improvement.md` § 3 and § 6 say what a review does with it). A carried line closes its key only once its pull request has merged, and leaves it held again if the pull request closed unmerged. Before it, no line ended a key, so each review read and held the same keys again: `asdlc-openspec-hpdd`'s notes held `.claude/skills/bead/SKILL.md#defect-found-on-the-way` at count 11, not sent to a group as no prompt's. Changing the word reopens every key closed under the old one, so a change rewrites them first. Decided 2026-10-05 by D-49 (asdlc-openspec-r6ha.6); the maintainer chose which held keys its first lines close.
promptReviewRecurrenceCountMeans: How many distinct runs must have shown a finding, those in the batch and those its held lines name, before a review proposes an edit for it, unless its severity is in `promptReviewMajorSeverities`. The reviewer's session applies it before the workflow runs and holds every finding below it, and `.claude/workflows/review-prompts.js` refuses one that reaches it. It is a choice, not a measurement: a research session on 2026-09-25 found no primary source for requiring a number of occurrences before an edit (asdlc-openspec-pnm). Where it loses: a one-off minor defect that costs an hour, and recurs a week later, is paid for twice before it is fixed. 1 proposes an edit for every finding, as D-08's review did. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-10 (asdlc-openspec-pnm).
promptReviewMajorSeveritiesMeans: The severities of a finding a review proposes on one run, skipping `promptReviewRecurrenceCount`. The severities are those `.claude/agents/branch-reviewer.md` § 2. Maintainability defines, so a prompt review and the branch review grade on one scale (the pull-request reviewer's until D-37 retired its rubric into that file). Adding `minor` removes the threshold; emptying the list makes every finding wait for a second run. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-10 (asdlc-openspec-pnm).
promptReviewSkepticsMeans: How many skeptics `.claude/workflows/review-prompts.js` sends to judge one proposed edit, by its finding's severity, once the file's agent has committed it. Each reads the branch's diff and answers upheld, refuted or unverified to two questions: had the prompt said this, would the runs have gone differently; and does the edit break another path through the prompt, or another caller of it. A majority of those sent decides, and a branch merges only when every edit on it is upheld (the workflow's header holds the mechanics). The counts copy `buildReviewSkeptics`. Lowering `blocker` below 3 lets one vote decide a blocker edit or a consolidation that every later run of the prompt reads. Decided 2026-09-26 with D-10 (asdlc-openspec-pnm). A consolidation (`.claude/agents/continuous-prompt-improvement.md` § How a prompt is consolidated) goes to the `blocker` count whatever its findings' severities, because a rule it loses is lost to every later run of the prompt: added 2026-09-26 with D-12 (asdlc-openspec-aa0). An unstated edit, to a file a report lists as changed and names in no change it states, goes to the `blocker` count too, since no finding gives it a severity: added 2026-10-04 with asdlc-openspec-d078. `major` lowered from 3 to 1 on 2026-09-28 by D-16 (asdlc-openspec-hsg), item 3, with `buildReviewSkeptics.major`, which the maintainer chose over the recommendation to leave both for asdlc-openspec-j09.11; a batch of 5 major findings now sends 5 skeptics, where it sent 15. Where it loses: a single vote now decides a major edit that every later run of the prompt reads, the case D-10 chose three to prevent.
promptReviewCaseLensesMeans: The lenses `.claude/workflows/author-prompt-cases.js` writes a candidate decision case through, one author each, for each settled finding a prompt review hands it: `recorded`, the situation as the run met it; `near-miss`, a neighbouring situation where the rule must not apply, which catches a broadened rule like the one point 7 of asdlc-openspec-aa0's analysis records; and `pressure`, the situation with a push toward the wrong option. A seed drawn from a prompt's section, with no run, gets no lens the workflow's library marks as needing a run, `recorded` today. The lens texts are the workflow's own, and a lens must exist there before this list names it: mise run workflows:selftest refuses one that does not. Proposed 2026-09-26 and confirmed 2026-10-03 by the maintainer (asdlc-openspec-7c1, `docs/decisions.md` § D-32). Where it loses: three authors for each of the first nine settled findings is 27 agents; dropping a lens saves one author per finding, and the cases that lens would have found.
promptReviewCaseRepetitionsMeans: How many times one decision case is answered with one text of its prompt, each answer an agent by the agentType `prompt-case-answerer`, shown the options in an order turned by one place at each repetition. `.claude/workflows/author-prompt-cases.js` stores a new case only when every one of these answers, with the trunk's text, chooses its expected option; `.claude/workflows/review-prompts.js` answers each stored case of a file an upheld branch changes this many times with the old text and as many with the new, and a case flips when a majority chose its expected option on the old text and not on the new (each workflow's header holds the mechanics). A review spends twice this many answers on each such case. The maintainer chose 3, with the stricter bar to store, on 2026-10-03 (asdlc-openspec-7c1, `docs/decisions.md` § D-32), over a majority for both: a case answered right 70% of the time on both texts is then stored 34% of the time, not 78%, and once stored flips by noise alone in 17% of the reviews that change its prompt; one answered right 95% of the time is stored 86% of the time and flips in 0.7%. Where it loses: a sound case answered right 80% of the time is turned away about half the time, so the bank grows more slowly. 5 cuts the flips by noise and costs 10 answers per case per review.
promptReviewMatchHeldMinProbabilityMeans: The probability at or above which the model's answer keys a finding of a prompt review with a key an earlier review holds. `scripts/match-held-findings.mjs` (`mise run prompt-review:match`) asks TypeSafe, for each finding of the batch, one Choice over the keys held about its prompt file and `none`, and a held key the model gives this much is the finding's key, decided by the model; under it, with `none` under `promptReviewMatchNoneMinProbability` too, the reviewer's session keys the finding as `.claude/agents/continuous-prompt-improvement.md` § 3 says, the model's answer recorded beside it. `.claude/workflows/review-prompts.js` refuses a finding the model keyed under it, and one the session keyed where the model's answer met it (each header holds the mechanics). It is above 0.5, so that only the model's top label can meet a threshold; the script refuses it otherwise. The 2026-09-29 experiment in the notes of asdlc-openspec-6yt.1 (jev-1.13.0, 45 held lines under 35 keys, 18 findings) proposed 0.8: the 10 findings labelled one with a held key drew 0.59 to 0.95 on it, and 0.8 for this key and `promptReviewMatchNoneMinProbability` decided 12 of the 18 right and sent the other 6 to the session, among them the one labelled related, at 0.77 on a held key. Measured again on 2026-10-05, with this script's question and `promptReviewMatchNoneOption`, over the tracker's 234 held lines under 142 keys, each finding a held reason left out (jev-1.13.0): of 29 reasons set against their own key, which another reason of it stood for, 18 took it at 0.8 and none another key, and 12 take it at 0.94; of 111 set against their file's other keys, 5 took one at 0.8, each a different failure in the same section of the same file, and none takes one at 0.94. The maintainer set it at 0.94 on 2026-10-05 (asdlc-openspec-6yt.1), choosing no wrong key in that sample over 6 more findings keyed by the model; 0.94 was read off the same 140 findings it is judged by, so it is provisional. Where it loses: the 6 of those 29 that drew 0.8 to 0.94 go to the session, which keys them freehand as before and can coin a key that drifts, the loss this match exists to cut; and two failures at one place in a prompt, worded alike, can still draw it, so the model gives the second the first's key and carries it past `promptReviewRecurrenceCount` a run early.
promptReviewMatchNoneMinProbabilityMeans: The probability of `none` at or above which the model's answer gives a finding of a prompt review a new key, which the reviewer's session names: `scripts/match-held-findings.mjs` routes on it as `promptReviewMatchHeldMinProbability` says, and `.claude/workflows/review-prompts.js` refuses a finding keyed new by the model under it, or one whose count names a held run. It is above 0.5, for the same reason. Provisional, from the same 18 findings: the 7 labelled new drew 0.75 to 0.99 on `none`, among them two findings of `.claude/skills/open-pr/SKILL.md` § 6 set against a held key of its § 7. Proposed in the note of 2026-09-29 on asdlc-openspec-6yt.1, set 2026-10-05 (asdlc-openspec-6yt.1). In the measurement `promptReviewMatchHeldMinProbabilityMeans` gives, 19 of the 111 left-out reasons with no key of their own drew `none` here and 34 at 0.7, and none of the 29 with one drew `none` at 0.7 or more; the other 87 went to the session with `promptReviewMatchHeldMinProbability` at 0.8, and 92 do at the 0.94 it is set to, since the 5 that took another key at 0.8 take none at 0.94; so on held lines most new findings are still keyed by hand. Where it loses: a recurring finding whose held reason words it unlike its new run can draw `none` at it, and is counted again from one, the loss this match exists to cut; raising it sends more findings to the session instead.
promptReviewMatchNoneOption: No option describes that failure: it is another step, or another place in the prompt, than every held finding, even where the two are worded alike or concern one section.
promptReviewMatchNoneOptionMeans: The text of the one option `scripts/match-held-findings.mjs` offers TypeSafe beside a finding's held keys, labelled `none`. The option set is the keys held about the finding's prompt file, each labelled by its key with a held reason as its text, as the 2026-09-29 experiment in the notes of asdlc-openspec-6yt.1 offered them, the script taking the reason of the key's held line of the highest count, and this. Its last clause names the case where a match loses, two failures at one place worded alike, so the model is told to tell them apart. Changing it changes what `none` draws, so the two thresholds' figures no longer hold until they are measured again. Set 2026-10-05 (asdlc-openspec-6yt.1).
promptReviewProseMinProbabilityMeans: The probability of yes at or above which one answer to a prose decision case meets it. `scripts/grade-prose-cases.mjs` (`mise run prompt-review:grade`) asks TypeSafe, for each answer `.claude/workflows/review-prompts.js` returns in `prose`, whether its text does what the case's `expected` says, and counts the answers that meet the case with each text; a case's outcome follows from those counts as a choice case's does from its right answers (the script's header holds the mechanics). The counts are listed in the review's pull request and keep no branch out, so this value moves what a person reads and never what merges. It is above 0 and at most 1; the script refuses it otherwise. Set 2026-10-10 (asdlc-openspec-1kie, `docs/decisions/asdlc-openspec-1kie.md` § Decision) at 0.5, where yes is likelier than no, with no measurement behind it: the session that set it had no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, so TypeSafe has not yet graded a prose answer here, and the value is provisional until a person with the key measures it on answers labelled by hand. Where it loses: a grader whose yes runs high on a text that drops what the case holds counts that text as meeting it, and the flip the counts were there to show reads as held.
rootCauseMaxFixesMeans: How many fixes that each failed a session makes against one failure before it makes no further fix and reports to the user what it tested, as `.claude/skills/root-cause/SKILL.md` § 6 says, which also says what counts as a fix that failed: a run that fixes past it is guessing, and the design may be what is wrong, which is the user's call. The skill reads it by key and spells no number. The maintainer set it on 2026-09-26 (asdlc-openspec-qfc) at 3, the number obra/superpowers' `systematic-debugging` skill uses at 8ca22db, which nothing in this repository has measured. Where it loses: a failure with several independent causes, each fix right but partial, stops at the third fix and waits on a person, although the run was converging. No gate holds it: a session reads it while it debugs, which no gate sees.
sessionReviewMaxFindingsMeans: The most findings the one adversarial reviewer reports in the review a session writes itself for a branch with code or a gate (`CLAUDE.md` § A workflow a session writes itself is bounded), so that it reports the ones that matter most and its skeptics stay few. A branch that changes only prompts or documents gets no such review. Decided 2026-09-28 by D-16 (asdlc-openspec-hsg), item 1, which the maintainer chose from a recommendation put with the case where it loses: a dedicated adversary that built doctored inputs found the code-fence defect in asdlc-openspec-j09.3's gate, and one general reviewer may miss that kind, which the pull-request reviewer, running nothing, will not catch.
sessionReviewSkepticsMeans: How many skeptics judge one finding of each severity in the review a session writes itself for a branch with code or a gate (`CLAUDE.md` § A workflow a session writes itself is bounded): the one skeptic's vote decides a blocker or a major finding, and a minor goes to the branch's author unjudged, as 0 says. The severities are those `.claude/agents/branch-reviewer.md` § 2. Maintainability defines. With `sessionReviewMaxFindings` findings, the review runs at most one reviewer and one skeptic for each, within `sessionWorkflowMaxAgents`. Decided 2026-09-28 by D-16 (asdlc-openspec-hsg), item 1. Where it loses: one skeptic that misreads a real major defect refutes it, where a majority of three would have outvoted it, and the branch reaches its pull request with the defect.
sessionWorkflowMaxAgentsMeans: The most agents a review or design workflow a session writes itself runs, outside `.claude/workflows/`, unless the user asks for more (`CLAUDE.md` § A workflow a session writes itself is bounded); an effort level or an orchestration default that says cost is no constraint does not raise it. Its value is the harness's workflow-size guideline that the session whose reviews led to D-16 ran under, which nothing in this repository bound (`bd show asdlc-openspec-hsg`). The review of a branch with code or a gate needs at most one reviewer and one skeptic for each of `sessionReviewMaxFindings` findings. Decided 2026-09-28 by D-16 (asdlc-openspec-hsg), item 4. Where it loses: a design question that needs more independent readings than this runs as two workflows, or waits for the user to ask for more.
